server.name: threatcluster
server.title: ThreatCluster
server.instructions: ThreatCluster is a threat-intelligence corpus: incident clusters (each cluster is one deduplicated story built from every source that covered it, with a threat score, timeline and extracted entities), entity profiles (threat actors, malware, tools, vendors, products, CVEs, countries, industries), CVE records with KEV / EPSS / exploit status, and ransomware leak-site victim listings. Always call a tool before stating a fact about a threat; never answer from memory. Every result carries `url` fields for citation and `cost` (credits spent). A free key has 100 credits a day and a 7-day lookback; call api_budget (free, no API call) to pace yourself. Use search_threats for named things, newest_threats for what is new, leak_site_victims for who was hit, lookup_entity for a profile, get_threat for depth on the 1-3 clusters that matter.

tools.name: search_threats
tools.title: Search incident clusters
tools.description: Keyword search over incident clusters (each cluster is one deduplicated story built from every source that covered it). Best for named things: actors, malware, vendors, products, CVE ids, companies, countries. Matching is literal: it tries the exact phrase, then all words together, then any word, and finally widens the time window if still under 3 hits; `matched_stage` says which stage matched. Use `alternatives` for spellings and synonyms (UK / United Kingdom / British). Costs 1 credit per term searched; at most 8 API calls per invocation, and `api_calls` in the result says how many were made. For one call that also covers entity profiles and the dark web use search_everything instead (5 credits).

alternatives.description: other names for the same thing, OR'd with query

days.description: only clusters with reporting in the last N days (free keys: up to 7)

tools.name: search_everything
tools.title: Search clusters, entities and the dark web
tools.description: One call across the whole corpus: incident clusters, entity profiles (actors, malware, vendors, CVEs) and dark-web ransomware listings that match the query. Costs 5 credits, so prefer search_threats (1 credit per term) when you only need clusters; use this when you do not know whether the name is an actor, a victim or a product, or when you want the dark-web hits too.

days.description: only results with activity in the last N days (free keys: up to 7)

limit.description: max clusters (entities and dark-web hits are capped the same way)

tools.name: newest_threats
tools.title: Newest incident clusters
tools.description: The newest incident clusters in a window, no keyword. Use for 'what happened today / this week', 'what's new', 'what should a SOC know'. `sort_by=new` lists by first report time; `sort_by=trending` ranks by how fast coverage is growing. 1 credit.

time_filter.description: window; 30d needs a paid key (free keys are clamped to 7d)

tools.name: get_threat
tools.title: Full record for one cluster
tools.description: Full record for one cluster returned by another tool: summary, timeline, the underlying articles with their source URLs, extracted entities and CVEs. Call this for the 1-3 clusters that matter before answering in depth. `identifier` is the cluster id, its 8-character short id, or the slug from a threatcluster.io/cluster/... URL. Set `include_iocs` to also fetch the cluster's validated indicators (+1 credit). 1 credit (2 with IOCs).

identifier.description: cluster id, 8-char short id, or slug

include_iocs.description: also return validated IOCs (domains, IPs, hashes, URLs) for the cluster

tools.name: leak_site_victims
tools.title: Ransomware leak-site victims
tools.description: Ransomware leak-site victim listings: who a group claims to have hit, when, sector, country. These are claims by the groups, not confirmed breaches. Returns the newest listings matching the filters plus a tally of every listing in the window by group, sector and country, so 'most active group' and 'most hit sector' questions are answered from the tally, not the sample. Use for any question about ransomware victims, a group's activity, or a sector / country being hit. 2 credits (listings + tally).

days.description: window in days (free keys: up to 7)

sector.description: e.g. Healthcare, Education, Financial Services, Manufacturing, Government

group.description: ransomware group name, e.g. qilin, akira, lockbit5

victim.description: substring of a victim organisation name or domain (matched client-side over the newest listings)

tools.name: lookup_entity
tools.title: Entity profile
tools.description: Profile of a threat actor, malware family, tool, company, product, country, industry or CVE as tracked in the corpus: how often it appears, first and last seen, the recent clusters and articles it appears in, and the entities it co-occurs with. Give `entity_type` when the name is ambiguous (a company that is also a malware name). 2 credits (name resolution + profile).

entity_type.description: optional: apt_group, ransomware_group, malware, tool, company, platform, cve, country, industry, campaign, attack_type, mitre_attack, domain, ipv4

tools.name: get_vulnerability
tools.title: CVE record
tools.description: One CVE record: description, CVSS, EPSS score and percentile, CISA KEV status with due date, known ransomware use, public exploit count and links, affected vendors and products, references. 1 credit.

tools.name: exploited_vulnerabilities
tools.title: Recently exploited CVEs
tools.description: CVEs published or updated in a window, filtered to the ones that matter: in CISA KEV (`kev_only`), with a public exploit (`has_exploit`), by severity, vendor or product. Use for 'what should we patch this week' and 'is anything in our stack being exploited'. 1 credit.

days.description: window in days (free keys: up to 7)

kev_only.description: only CVEs in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue

has_exploit.description: only CVEs with a public exploit

vendor.description: CPE vendor, e.g. microsoft, cisco, fortinet

product.description: CPE product, e.g. windows, ios, fortios

tools.name: trending_entities
tools.title: Trending entities
tools.description: Which threat actors, ransomware crews, malware families, tools, vendors, products, CVEs, countries and industries are rising in the corpus over a window, with mention counts and the change against the previous window. Indicator types (hashes, IPs, wallets) are left out unless named in `entity_types`. 1 credit.

time_filter.description: window; 30d needs a paid key (free keys are clamped to 7d)

tools.name: api_budget
tools.title: Remaining API budget
tools.description: Credits and rate-limit state from the headers of the most recent API responses in this session, plus what has been spent so far. No API call is made and nothing is charged; call it to pace yourself before a burst of lookups. Free keys: 100 credits a day, 30 requests a minute, budget refills at 00:00 UTC.

prompts.name: threatcluster_analyst
prompts.title: ThreatCluster analyst
prompts.description: Answer a threat-intelligence question over ThreatCluster's corpus with the tools, citing every fact with the returned URLs.

arguments.name: question
arguments.description: the question to answer; leave empty to just load the analyst rules

prompts.template:
You are ThreatCluster's analyst assistant, answering over ThreatCluster's own corpus: incident clusters (deduplicated stories with sources and timelines), entity profiles, CVE records and ransomware leak-site listings, reached through the threatcluster MCP tools.

Today is {today}. Date words mean: "today" = last 24h; "this week" / "past week" = last 7 days; "this month" / "recent" / "lately" = last 30 days (say "in the last 30 days" in the answer). Say what period you searched. A free key sees the last 7 days; if a result says `lookback_days: 7`, say so when the question asked for more.

Rules:
1. Always call tools first; never answer from memory. Use search_threats for named things, newest_threats for "what's new", leak_site_victims for ransomware victims or a sector/country being hit, lookup_entity for an actor/malware/vendor/CVE profile, get_vulnerability / exploited_vulnerabilities for CVEs, get_threat for depth on the 1-3 clusters that matter.
2. If a windowed search returns nothing, widen the window once (about 4x) before concluding there is nothing; then say plainly that nothing was found in the asked period and offer the nearest older reporting, dated.
3. Every fact you state must be followed by a citation: the `url` of the tool result it came from, as a Markdown link on the cluster, entity, victim or CVE it names. A tally (counts by group/sector) is cited with the listing URLs it summarises. Never invent a URL or a fact. Passages of general knowledge must be marked "(general knowledge)" and carry no link.
4. Leak-site listings are claims by the groups, not confirmed breaches; say so once when you use them.
5. Be concise and specific: dates, names, numbers. Markdown with short bullets, under 250 words unless the user asks for depth. No preamble.
6. Economy: leak_site_victims alone answers who-hit-whom and most-active questions from its tally; do not search clusters per group afterwards. Prefer one well-chosen call per fact you need; every result reports `cost`, and api_budget (free) tells you what is left. Two rounds of calls is normal, four is the limit.{question_block}
